dedupe_keys.name: natural water retention measures in the altovicentino area life beware

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes seven Natural Water Retention Measures built in 2019-2020 in the municipalities of Santorso and Marano Vicentino in the Altovicentino area of Veneto, Italy, under the LIFE BEWARE project, to reduce increasingly frequent pluvial flooding. Measures include a rain garden and an underdrain bioretention area at a car park, and a swale with a live fascine and hidden pipe intercepting hill runoff above houses, among others. Before the appraisal a hydrological-hydraulic simulation model mapped flooded areas with and without the measures for 2-, 5- and 30-year return periods; the benefit-cost analysis over 30 years counted avoided flood damage, drought benefits to farming and drinking water saved, and found a net present value of about 3.63 million euros, a benefit-cost ratio of 2.30 and an internal rate of return of 14.1 percent. The seven measures cost 362,276 euros of a project budget of about 2.1 million euros. The page, published in 2020 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the project site and deliverables. Caveats: the appraisal includes further measures expected from private and public actors, and upscaling depends on funding. It illustrates simulation-based appraisal of nature-based flood hazard reduction for climate adaptation; related records are the Gomeznarro Park and Serchio nature-based solutions case studies and ERA5.
name: Natural Water Retention Measures in the Altovicentino area (LIFE BEWARE)
